nodes.label: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Preserves successive experiments: the original $10,000 pilot lost $23.60, the $1,000 guarded baseline lost $11.30, and settled-cash variants A and B/C lost $11.026 and $18.70 respectively. These are separate models and account configurations, not cumulative P&L.

nodes.label: Frozen historical replay pilot
nodes.rationale: Uses FTFT, SES and TE over four September sessions with a 1.5-ATR stop, 2R target, fifteen-minute hold, and engineering assumptions for costs and latency. Four FTFT trades lost $23.60; 424 tests, deterministic repetition and 26 artifact checks establish offline implementation behavior rather than profitability.

nodes.label: Running-peak drawdown guard and unknown equity
nodes.rationale: The historical $1,000 account uses a fixed $100 threshold below the running equity peak. Unknown valuation blocks new risk, and threshold detection cancels entries and routes exits; gaps, latency and capacity can still overshoot. The baseline observed $43 drawdown and 40.915 seconds of unknown equity, so observed marks do not certify a continuous maximum loss.

nodes.label: Settled cash and T+1 funding model
nodes.rationale: Separates settled cash, reservations and signed unsettled proceeds. Sales remain in equity but cannot finance another intraday round trip; calendar-based availability is modeled at 09:30 Eastern on T+1. Structural infeasibility is rejected before reservation. Settlement transfers do not create profits, and actual broker posting time is unknown.

nodes.label: Fifty-share planning liquidity cap
nodes.rationale: Maximum-allocation variant C still bought 50 FTFT shares because 25% of the observed 200-share planning bid size bound quantity below cash capacity 199 and risk capacity 242. The $247.60 deployment and identical B/C outcomes identify the binding model constraint without establishing actual market capacity.

nodes.label: Prospective recording and clock uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Twenty newly acquired sessions were minute-only, and the 180.018-second prospective capture retained 743 records. With unmeasured local clock accuracy and 382 negative receipt-minus-provider timestamp differences among 718 quote/trade observations, the capture cannot calibrate execution latency or supply an execution-ready holdout.
